title: Enforcing C/C++ Type and Scope at Runtime for Control-Flow and Data-Flow Integrity
problem: Control-flow hijacking and data-oriented attacks exploit pointers being used in unintended ways, violating their original scope or declared types, potentially leaking sensitive information like SSL keys. Existing defenses face significant performance challenges due to the abundance of data pointers requiring monitoring.
motivation: Data-oriented attacks represent a critical security threat requiring practical defenses that achieve control-flow and data-flow integrity without excessive performance overhead.
method: The system enforces C/C++ type and scope constraints at runtime through program instrumentation. Runtime checks validate that each pointer access conforms to its declared type and original scope, preventing type confusion and scope violations that enable data-oriented attacks.
key_novelty: Unified runtime enforcement of both type and scope constraints specifically targeting data-oriented attack prevention in C/C++ programs.
contributions: Runtime mechanism for enforcing C/C++ type and scope constraints on pointers
Defense against data-oriented attacks with practical performance characteristics
Integrated control-flow and data-flow integrity approach
primary_theme: Runtime type and scope enforcement for attack prevention
